title: pilot-legal-cfo-pocket-deck-wip
content:
Slide 1 — One-line purpose:
Quick-pocket deck for SEs to run a short procurement/CFO-focused pilot conversation and close reserved/dedicated commitments. NOT customer-facing final — field script + math + quick legal talking points.

Slide 2 — TL;DR for SEs (30s pitch to CFO/Procurement):
- We provide predictable inference costs with committed capacity + fallbacks.
- Pilot structure: 4-week technical pilot (test traffic + perf), 30-day pricing guardrail for costing, and optional Reserved Capacity LOI.
- Key ask: access to procurement for a 1:1 capex vs opex comparison and a 2–3 person technical contact.

Slide 3 — Why this deck exists (problem we solve for CFOs):
- Procurement hates surprise variable spend and unpredictable SLAs.
- CFO needs: clear spend envelope, downgrade/exit paths, auditability.
- This deck gives a tight script + one-page model to make procurement say yes faster.

Slide 4 — Pilot blueprint (recommended):
- Week 0: NDA + SOW-lite (1 page) + initial traffic sampling agreement.
- Weeks 1–3: Technical validation (latency, throughput, quality). Daily 10–15min sync.
- Week 4: Cost run & ops handoff. Provide a 30-day forecast for production profiles.
- Deliverable: Pilot report (performance, cost projection, recommended commit tier).

Slide 5 — Pricing guardrail (the simple model) — talk track and numbers (example):
- Assumption: 20 req/s peak, 10M tokens/month.
- Hosted variable cost estimate: $X per token (show ballpark).
- Dedicated reserved option: monthly committed GPU pool = $Y (discount vs hosted at 25–40%).
- CFO script: "We can lock a predictable ceiling with reserved capacity and a 30-day ramp-down clause to protect you."

Slide 6 — Procurement-friendly clauses to offer (speaker notes):
- Billing cap (monthly ceiling) with auto-notify at 80% usage.
- 30-day rollback: customer can reduce reserved tier once after Go-Live with prorated credits.
- Audit logs and token-level spend reports delivered weekly during pilot.
- Data controls: option for VPC/private plane or SOC2 addendum.

Slide 7 — Quick rebuttals to legal redlines (bullet bank):
- IP/data: default position -> customer retains prompt+data ownership, Redwood processes ephemeral inference outputs; propose standard DPA.
- SLA credits: use credit-based approach rather than termination; keeps pilot aligned.
- Security scans: propose fortnightly evidence package vs unlimited on-demand scans to limit noise.

Slide 8 — 60s CFO script + one-pager leave-behind (talking points):
- "We align economics to usage. For pilot, we cap your spend and provide weekly visibility. If you commit, we give a discount + predictable throughput guarantees."
- Leave-behind includes: one-line value, top 3 risks + mitigations, 2–3 pricing rows for fast decision.

Slide 9 — Field play examples (realistic snippets):
- Procurement objection: "We can't commit now."
  - Response: "We can run a 4-week pilot with a spend cap and an LOI placeholder for capacity; only convert when you see the forecast numbers."
- CFO question: "How do we avoid overpaying for idle GPUs?"
  - Response: "Autoscaling policies + burst credits; we include a usage profile analysis in pilot report to right-size the pool."

Slide 10 — Technical appendix (for SE to hand to infra contact):
- Data flows (sketch), KMS/HSM integration options, VPC peering checklist, expected artifact: per-token telemetry, request trace ids.
- Notes-to-self: attach sample perf logs (we'll include in pilot repo).

Slide 11 — Negotiation cheat sheet (step-by-step):
- Step 1: Align on top-of-funnel: decision maker + legal contact + technical contact.
- Step 2: Send SOW-lite + pilot SLOs (latency P95, error budget).
- Step 3: Run pilot; send weekly cost snapshots.
- Step 4: 1-week before pilot end, propose commit tier with a simple 3-row price table and benefit bullets.

Slide 12 — Sample 3-row price table (verbal template):
- Row A: No commit — Hosted usage, per-token pricing (best for <X tokens).
- Row B: Small commit — Dedicated small GPU pool, 20% discount, recommended for 10–40M tokens/month.
- Row C: Enterprise reserve — multi-region pool + longer term SLA + 35–45% discount.

Slide 13 — Metrics to collect during pilot (for CFO story):
- Weekly spend and projected month-end spend (USD).
- Latency P95 and error rate.
- Tokens served and cache hit rate.
- Estimated committed savings vs hosted baseline.

Slide 14 — Leave-behind: one-page risk matrix for procurement (example layout):
- Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Ownership
- Data loss | Low | High | DPA + KMS | Engineering
- Unexpected spend | Medium | Medium | Billing cap + alerts | Finance ops
- Downtime | Low | High | SLA + fallback plan | SRE

Slide 15 — Objection answer bank (copyable lines for SEs):
- "We don't want vendor lock-in" -> "Models are versioned and customers can download model snapshots for on-prem if needed; rolling fallback to open weights is an option."
- "How do we validate results?" -> "We ship a prompt suite and QA harness and include regression alerting during pilot."

Slide 16 — Internal ops checklist (TODOs for SEs before pilot kickoff):
- Create pilot folder under GH repo (checklist template link).
- Request procurement email thread and legal contact.
- Pre-fill SOW-lite with dates and cap.
- Set up weekly calendar invites with technical checkpoints.

Slide 17 — Post-pilot close flow (recommended):
- SE: Prepare 1-pager recommendation + cost delta table.
- CSM/Account Exec: Run commercial runbook (discounts, contract terms).
- Legal: Sign agreed SOW + DPA.

Slide 18 — Notes to self / rough TODOs (raw):
- Add small sample spreadsheet for token math (make a simple formula row).
- Attach 2 anonymized pilot case studies (ask CS).
- Iterate LOI language with legal (JIRA: JIRA-PLT-314).

Slide 19 — Quick links and artifacts to attach when sharing with customer:
- Pilot SOW-lite template (GH link), sample pilot report, weekly cost snapshot CSV, data handling one-pager.

Slide 20 — Next steps for this draft (internal):
- Gather anonymized pilot numbers from CS (owners: Marcus + Elena) — due 2026-03-17.
- Legal to review rollback clause language (owner: Omar) — due 2026-03-14.
- Iterate slide copy for a 2-slide CFO leave-behind (owner: Priya) — due 2026-03-12.

Footer: this deck is intentionally lightweight for rapid field use. Keep it short, use the cheat lines, and do NOT over-document in the first customer call. Mark as internal and draft.
